batch.title: General science sampler
batch.material: Fabricated sample Questions on general science, written for trying PencilMark

stem.text: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere by volume?

rationale.text: Correct: nitrogen is about 78% of dry air.
Oxygen is about 21%, the second largest share.

misconception.text: Assuming the gas we breathe for respiration must be the most abundant one.

rationale.text: Carbon dioxide is well under 1% of the atmosphere.

misconception.text: Overestimating CO₂ because of how often it is discussed in climate news.

rationale.text: Argon is about 0.9%, the third largest share.

explanation.text: Dry air is roughly 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 0.9% argon, with carbon dioxide and other gases making up the rest.

stem.text: A ball is dropped from rest. Ignoring air resistance, roughly how fast is it falling after 2 seconds?

rationale.text: That is the speed after 1 second.

misconception.text: Treating g as a speed rather than a rate of change of speed.

rationale.text: Correct: v = g × t ≈ 9.8 m/s² × 2 s ≈ 20 m/s.
This squares the time, which applies to distance, not speed.

misconception.text: Mixing up v = gt with d = ½gt².

content.text: It falls at a constant speed, so it depends only on its mass

rationale.text: Without air resistance, every object accelerates at the same rate, whatever its mass.

misconception.text: The everyday intuition that heavier objects fall faster.

explanation.text: In free fall the speed grows by about 9.8 m/s every second, so after 2 seconds it is about 20 m/s. {{opt:opt_40}} confuses speed with the distance formula.

stem.text: Which of these are found in a typical plant cell but not in a typical animal cell? Select all that apply.

rationale.text: Correct: plant cells have a cellulose cell wall; animal cells do not.
Correct: chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis in plant cells.
Both plant and animal cells have mitochondria.

misconception.text: Believing plants get all their energy from chloroplasts and so need no mitochondria.

rationale.text: Every cell has a cell membrane, inside the wall in plants.

misconception.text: Thinking the cell wall replaces the membrane.

explanation.text: Cell walls and chloroplasts (and usually a large central vacuole) set plant cells apart. Mitochondria and the cell membrane are shared by both.

stem.text: Which of these are chemical changes? Select all that apply.

rationale.text: Correct: iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide, a new substance.
Melting changes only the state; it is still water.

misconception.text: Treating any visible change of appearance as a chemical change.

rationale.text: Correct: combustion produces carbon dioxide, water and ash.
Dissolving is physical: evaporating the water gives the sugar back.

misconception.text: Thinking that because the sugar disappears, it has become something else.

rationale.text: Correct: heat drives reactions in the batter that cannot be undone.

explanation.text: A chemical change makes new substances and is usually hard to reverse. Melting and dissolving are physical changes: the substance stays the same.

stem.text: Which planet in our solar system is closest to the Sun?

rationale.text: Correct: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.
Venus is second, though it is the hottest planet.

misconception.text: Assuming the hottest planet must be the closest.

rationale.text: Earth is third.
One of the listed planets is the closest.

explanation.text: Mercury is closest; Venus is hotter because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.

stem.text: Sound travels faster in air than in water.

rationale.text: Sound is about four times faster in water than in air.

misconception.text: Thinking a denser medium must slow sound down.

rationale.text: Correct: about 343 m/s in air against about 1,480 m/s in water.

explanation.text: Sound moves faster through water because water resists compression far more strongly than air does.

stem.text: Pure water at sea level boils at 100 °C.

rationale.text: Correct: at standard sea-level pressure, pure water boils at 100 °C.
The boiling point changes with pressure, but at sea level it is 100 °C.

misconception.text: Remembering that boiling point varies and overgeneralising to sea level.

explanation.text: Boiling point depends on pressure: on a high mountain water boils below 100 °C.

stem.text: Humans and other mammals are warm-blooded, keeping a roughly constant body temperature.

rationale.text: Correct: mammals regulate their body temperature internally.
Mammals are endotherms, unlike most reptiles.

explanation.text: Mammals and birds are endotherms: they generate heat to hold a steady temperature.
